c1.hypothesis: Two changes. (1) Start an attack only when we have at least 8 units and our army power is at least 1.4 times the remembered enemy army power plus 4. Enemy power is summed from enemy combat units we legally saw in the last 3600 frames; dead units are removed from the list. Fall back to the rally when our power drops below 0.9 times theirs or the army falls under 4 units. Always attack at 30 or more
c1.expectation: Against Steamhammer and BananaBrain: fewer early army wipes, a higher healthy-army peak (more than 15 instead of 9-17), a better exchange ratio (above 0.4), and the Cybernetics Core done before frame 6000. PylonPuller should still be won by the same late push, since its army is small and the gate opens easily. Main risk: more time spent at home might raise lock_defense time.

c11.diagnosis:
BananaBrain (match-43) and the Steamhammer retest (match-44) were both lost the same way: a zealot rush wiped out the main base. Our 5 Zealots stood against 6–7 enemy Zealots. Worker defense has a hard rule in pickDefenseTarget and workerDefense: once army.size() >= 5, non-building targets are skipped or defenders are released with reason "army". That rule ignores which side is stronger.

The log
c11.hypothesis: Release worker defenders, or skip unit targets, at army >= 5 only when threatPower <= homePower*1.1. When the enemy outguns the home army, 4 Probes keep joining the fight next to our Zealots. They add damage and soak hits in the early 5v6/6v7 Zealot fights. Nothing changes when our army is stronger, so later-game and macro behavior stay the same.
c11.expectation: Against BananaBrain and Steamhammer zealot rushes, Probes stay engaged through frames 6000–7200. The aim is to hold the main at about 6900 instead of collapsing: at least 10 workers alive at 8400 and past the 8400 cutoff, for a score above 30 and possibly a win. PylonPuller (the mid-game DT fight) and the Steamhammer macro win should be unchanged.
